Anyone with access to the host, logs, monitoring, backups, or adjacent operational systems may infer that a specific user submitted identity documents or when such submissions occurred.
assumptions: Assumes backend/uploads/images is reachable by administrators, support tooling, backup systems, scanners, or other components that can observe filesystem changes or related operational artifacts.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node selection is reasonably grounded by retrieved context for D.2 (application side-effects), but the exact observability depends on deployment and operational controls.

title: Uploaded ID images in the filesystem may be exposed to unauthorized parties
description: This flow stores highly sensitive identity-document images in a filesystem-backed datastore. If the directory is web-accessible, misconfigured, shared with other processes, insufficiently access-controlled, or included in broad backups/logging, unauthorized parties could access the images and learn directly identifying personal information from them.
assumptions: Assumes the uploaded idImage contains directly identifying data and that storage/access controls may be imperfect or broader than strictly necessary.

title: Retention of ID images on disk may exceed user expectations or legal necessity
description: Persisting uploaded identity-document images in backend/uploads/images can violate data minimization, purpose limitation, storage limitation, or deletion obligations if files are kept longer than necessary, reused for secondary purposes, or not removed from backups and replicas after the original purpose is fulfilled.
assumptions: Assumes no clearly enforced retention/deletion policy is tied to this storage operation and that the images are personal data subject to privacy/legal constraints.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance is a plausible privacy threat for this storage flow, but the exact subtree citation is approximate due to missing retrieved threat-tree details for Nc.

title: The presence and organization of stored ID images can enable profiling of users
description: A collection of uploaded idImage files in a dedicated filesystem location can enable inference about which users underwent identity verification, when they did so, how frequently documents were replaced, or which categories of users require such uploads. Even if filenames are indirect, metadata and directory structure may support singling out or profiling.
assumptions: Assumes filenames, timestamps, folder structure, or linked metadata can be correlated with user accounts or transactions by someone with datastore visibility.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness is not applicable here; this is intended as linkability/profiling-related identifiability under U, but the exact node citation is approximate without the full threat tree context.

title: Uploaded video presence can be detected via filesystem side effects
description: Storing an uploaded video in backend/uploads creates a persistent file-system artifact. An attacker or co-resident component with access to file names, timestamps, directory listings, storage growth, backup traces, or monitoring logs may detect that a specific user action occurred (e.g., a video upload), even without reading the video contents.
assumptions: Assumes some party beyond the intended processor can observe filesystem metadata, storage utilization, backups, or operational traces related to backend/uploads.

title: Stored video files and metadata may expose user identity
description: Video uploads written to the file system may contain direct identifiers in the content or in associated file metadata, and filenames or directory conventions may embed account, session, or device identifiers. If file-system access is broader than necessary, the datastore can reveal the uploader's identity.
assumptions: Assumes uploaded videos or their stored metadata/filenames may contain identifiers and that storage access control is imperfect or broader than strictly necessary.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement; the retrieved context did not provide identity-specific node ids for this flow.

title: Stored uploads may enable linking multiple videos to the same user
description: If backend/uploads uses stable naming patterns, shared directory locations, account-specific paths, or retained metadata, multiple uploaded videos can be correlated and linked to the same individual or device over time.
assumptions: Assumes storage structure, naming, or metadata is stable enough to correlate uploads, and an observer can access those artifacts.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement; the retrieved context did not provide linkability-specific node ids for this flow.

title: Uploader may be unable to deny a video submission if durable storage records are retained
description: When /api/videos stores a video in persistent backend/uploads, the system may retain durable evidence such as file timestamps, hashes, filenames, or audit records tying the upload event to a user or device. These records can reduce the user's plausible deniability regarding having submitted the video.
assumptions: Assumes the application or surrounding platform records upload-associated metadata that can be attributed to a user or device.
uncertainty_note: Whether this is a privacy problem depends on whether deniability is a desired property in the system; node id chosen by best judgement.

title: Stored video content may disclose sensitive personal information
description: Uploaded videos often contain rich personal data such as faces, voices, locations, surroundings, health indicators, or other special-category information. Persisting them in backend/uploads increases the risk that the datastore discloses more personal information than necessary if access, retention, or minimization controls are weak.
assumptions: Assumes videos can contain sensitive personal data and that storage protections or retention limits may be insufficient.

title: Users may be unaware that uploaded videos are persistently stored in backend/uploads
description: The flow description indicates uploaded videos are stored on the backend file system. If users are not clearly informed about this persistence, its duration, backup handling, or who can access the files, they may be unaware of the collection and storage of their personal data.
assumptions: Assumes notice about storage location, persistence, access, and retention is absent or unclear.

title: Persisting uploads on the filesystem may violate data minimization or retention requirements
